session_start.title: [akmon] Role declaration
session_start.format_line: Before doing project work, state which role you are operating in, and restate it whenever you switch. Format: `🧭 role: <name> — <focus>`.
session_start.develop_line: - DEVELOP (build the project), agents and the roles they work in: {{agents}}
session_start.operate_line: - OPERATE (run/use from outside), agents and the roles they work in: {{agents}}
session_start.pick_by_operation: Pick the role (never an agent name) by operation: decompose an existing thing → review · construct a new structure/decision → architect · realize a decided structure in code → engineer. If unclear, ask.
session_start.pick_generic: Pick the role the task calls for, one of the roles listed above, never an agent name; if unclear, ask.
session_start.delegation_line: Delegation is the default for non-atomic work: before the first repository sweep, edit, or test run, decompose the task and delegate every independent sub-step to available subagents. Keep only decomposition, routing, synthesis, and owner dialogue in the orchestrator. Skip delegation only when the task is atomic or the harness exposes no subagents; state the reason.
session_start.memory_line: Also: read `{{root_name}}/memory/` at session start (project memory).

role_on_code_message:
[akmon] Role check — you are editing project code.
Editing code is **realization** → the `engineer` role. Discriminator: decompose an existing thing → `review` · construct a new structure/decision → `architect` · realize a decided structure in code → `engineer`. If you were assessing (`review`) or designing (`architect`) — or no role is declared — this is a switch: declare `🧭 role: engineer — <focus>` and follow its pipeline (code-flow + pre-commit: tests + lint mandatory before "done") before continuing. Restate the role on every switch (roles/README.md).
Design→code hand-off: before writing code, confirm the task is **landed in `{{tasks}}`** with a link to its design (design-flow step 8 Hand-off), and **re-read the backlog** to sequence it against other work (code-flow step 1 Take) — a cold engineer session must be able to pick this task from `{{tasks}}` alone.
analysis_before_mutation_message:
[akmon] Analysis-before-mutation check — you are editing a planning/design doc (backlog / design / ADR / requirements / akmon process).
Role: **assessing what is** (problems, state, conformance) is `review`; **constructing the design** (options, contracts, the chosen structure) is `architect`. Declare the role (`🧭 role: <name> — <focus>`) and restate it on a switch (roles/README.md).
If this turn is analysis-only — the owner asked you to analyze, explain, review, compare options, or identify what remains — STOP: report findings + a recommendation in chat and get explicit confirmation ("write it" / "record it" / "make the change") before editing. If the request was already an edit command, proceed. Rule: guardrails/_common.md § Analysis before mutation.
drift_score_text: a drift score of {{score}} (an edit or shell call counts 1, a read ½, the first {{grace}} calls of a stretch nothing)
delegation_roster: `k_explorer` · mechanical edits / doc-sync / test scaffolds → `k_mechanic` · gate loops → `k_validator` · code under a decided contract → `k_implementer` · load-bearing analysis → `k_reasoner`
delegation_nudge_message:
[akmon] Delegation check — {{drift_score}} since the last subagent delegation.
Delegation is the default: route by task kind (MODEL.md § Capability tiers; guardrails/_common.md § Route by task kind). Exploration/summaries → {{roster}}.
If this genuinely is orchestrator work (decompose / route / synthesize / owner dialogue), carry on — this reminder is advisory and fires once per drift episode (a subagent delegation re-arms it).
delegation_ask_message:
[akmon] Sustained delegation drift — {{drift_score}} with no subagent delegation. A read never carries this ask, so it lands on a call that changes something (guardrails/_common.md § Route by task kind).
Route the next steps to a `k_*` delegate — exploration/summaries → {{roster}} — or confirm this is genuinely one of the orchestrator's reserved four (decompose · route · synthesize · owner dialogue) to proceed.
Fires once per drift episode (a subagent delegation re-arms it).
privilege_escalation_reason: Privilege-escalation guardrail: 'sudo' is never run by the agent. If elevated access is genuinely required, ask the owner to run the command themselves.
git_commit_no_ai_trailer_reason: Commit guardrail: no AI 'Co-Authored-By' trailer — the committer is the human. Remove it and retry.
git_commit_push_tag_merge_reason: Commit guardrail: the owner owns publishing. push and tag are the owner's everywhere, a linked worktree's own branch included — confirm this is explicitly requested.
git_commit_history_reason: Commit guardrail: git {{subcommand}} writes history in {{where}}. The agent writes history only inside a linked worktree, on that worktree's own branch; anywhere else it is the owner's — confirm explicitly, or run it in a worktree.
git_commit_ref_reason: Commit guardrail: git {{subcommand}} moves, renames or deletes {{target}}. The agent moves, renames or deletes no ref but its own `_aitna/` job branches, and removes or moves no worktree, in any directory — confirm explicitly, or leave it to the owner.
git_commit_ref_target_stdin: the refs named on its standard input
git_commit_where_unresolved: a directory the guard cannot resolve from the command text

git_ref_unconditional.replace: the refs it writes under refs/replace/

escalated_ask_suffix: [escalated ask→deny: the run is unattended — permission_mode={{permission_mode}}, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED={{attended}} — so 'ask' cannot be trusted to reach the owner (ADR-0025/D06, C31) — re-run from an attended session if this was genuinely intended.]
stale_guardrail_notice: ⚠ akmon: the rules in {{root_name}}/.akmon/ are not the ones this session's akmon ships ({{names}}). Run `akmon sync`, then start a new session — the rules are @-imported once at session start, so this session keeps the stale copy.
